title: Expiry from an ISO-8601 amount

blocks.text: A storage service keeps each file for a retention amount read from its configuration, written in ISO-8601: `P6M`, `P1Y2M3D`, `PT90M`, `PT2H30M`.
Write `Retention.expiresAt(ZonedDateTime created, String amount)`, the moment the file expires:

items: An amount with a time part (after a `T`, as in `PT24H` or `P1DT12H`) is exact elapsed time: `PT24H` is 24 hours and `P1DT12H` is 36 hours.

An amount with **only date parts** (`P...` with no `T`) is a calendar amount, counted on the calendar in `created`'s zone. That holds for `P1D` too: one day later is the same wall-clock time the next day.
Text that is not such an amount is **refused with `IllegalArgumentException`**.

blocks.text: So `P1M` is a month and `PT1M` is a minute.

cases.says: P6M adds six calendar months and PT90M adds ninety minutes, so P1M and PT1M differ.
P1D on the day the clocks spring forward keeps the wall-clock time, while PT24H adds 24 hours.
Text such as 6 months or an empty string is refused with IllegalArgumentException.

concepts: Duration and Period read and write ISO-8601 text: PT2H30M is a Duration and P1Y2M3D a Period, so the T decides minutes versus months.
